what: HER2, also called ERBB2 or human epidermal growth factor receptor 2, is a gene.
According to the CIViC gene summary in this snapshot, ERBB2 is amplified and/or overexpressed in 20-30% of invasive breast carcinomas.
intro.test_report: If a test report mentions HER2, it is recording a finding about this gene. This page lists public FDA companion diagnostics that look for HER2, and the therapies and trials in this snapshot that use HER2 as a selection criterion. That mention is not a diagnosis or a treatment decision on its own.

lines.text: Ado-Trastuzumab Emtansine (KADCYLA) is a HER2-targeted antibody and microtubule inhibitor conjugate. The FDA label lists this use: as a single agent, for: the treatment of patients with HER2-positive, metastatic breast cancer who previously received trastuzumab and a taxane, separately or in combination. Patients should have either: received prior therapy for metastatic disease, or developed disease recurrence during or within six months. An EMA record for Kadcyla lists the status as Authorised, with an authorisation date of 19/09/2013.

Fam-trastuzumab deruxtecan (ENHERTU) is a HER2-directed antibody and topoisomerase inhibitor conjugate. The FDA label lists this use: HER2-Positive Early Breast Cancer as neoadjuvant treatment of adult patients with HER2-positive (IHC 3+ or ISH+) Stage II or III breast cancer, as determined by an FDA-authorized test followed by a taxane, trastuzumab, and pertuzumab (THP). as adjuvant treatment of adult patients with HER2-positiv. An EMA record for Enhertu lists the status as Authorised, with an authorisation date of 10/12/2020.

Lapatinib is listed on an FDA label in this snapshot. The label mentions tablets. The FDA label lists this use: Lapatinib tablets are indicated in combination with: capecitabine for the treatment of patients with advanced or metastatic breast cancer whose tumors overexpress human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) and who have received prior therapy, including an anthracycline, a taxane, and trastuzumab. An EMA record for Tyverb lists the status as Authorised, with an authorisation date of 10/06/2008.

Margetuximab (MARGENZA) is a HER2/neu receptor antagonist. The FDA label lists this use: in combination with chemotherapy, for the treatment of adult patients with metastatic HER2-positive breast cancer who have received two or more prior anti-HER2 regimens, at least one of which was for metastatic disease MARGENZA is a HER2/neu receptor antagonist indicated, in combination with.

CIViC’s summary is: ERBB2 G292R may be sensitive to HER2 inhibitors, but data are very limited. The record lists evidence level TIER_II_LEVEL_D and status SUBMITTED. This is not an FDA approval.
